extracted.intended_audience: OPQA reviewers and USPTO patent examiners performing MRF compliance reviews of office-action rejections
extracted.subtask_short: OPQA compliance review of patent rejections
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for OPQA (MRF) reviewers to determine whether various types of office-action rejections (35 U.S.C. 102, 103, 112(a) enablement, 112(a) written description) are procedurally and substantively compliant and to record characteristics, root causes, examples, and suggested feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Were all the 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection(s) in compliance?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether each 103 rejection properly identifies the claim(s), the statute/subparagraph (as appropriate), and is supported by sufficient evidence to establish a prima facie case of obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes or No. Consult the statutory compliance standard and scenarios for guidance. If No, continue to detailed questions identifying the noncompliant claims and reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applied statute identification (102/103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which statute/subparagraph the applied prior art rejection(s) was made under (check all that apply): 35 USC 102 and/or 35 USC 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When either the claim(s) or the statute is the basis of the noncompliance, note the incorrect statute/subparagraph. If a disclosure is prior art but under a different subparagraph, check the incorrect-subparagraph box rather than 'disclosure not prior art.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to properly identify rejected claim(s) and/or statute (103 §4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection does not properly identify the rejected claim(s) and/or identify the correct statute/subparagraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This box is for failures in identification only. Do not use this box when the problem is lack of evidentiary support (use 4(c)). Do not use to capture omitted rejections—raise omitted rejections separately. Explanations should avoid rhetorical questions and personalization; explain basis for noncompliance tied to identification failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure does not qualify as prior art (103 §4(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure relied upon as the basis of the rejection is not prior art under any statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the disclosure is prior art but not as identified, do not check this box; instead check the incorrect-subparagraph box. Provide an explanation why the disclosure is not available as prior art. Avoid rhetorical questioning and personalization; focus on assessment of the work product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection fails to provide sufficient evidence to establish prima facie obviousness (103 §4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection applied fails to reasonably establish a prima facie case for obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If checked, the reviewer must identify the basis for insufficient evidence by checking at least one of 4(c)(i)–4(c)(v). Consult statutory compliance scenarios for examples and threshold determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings of fact not properly articulated and/or evidenced (103 §4(c)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection's findings of fact (mapping of claim limitations to prior-art teachings) are incomplete or missing (e.g., missing limitation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the teachings relied on are not found within the references, check this box. If checked, one of 4(c)(i)(A)1-3 and one of 4(c)(i)(B) or (C) must also be checked. The finding of facts is directed to correlation of claim limitations to teachings in the references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation to primary reference / assumption of primary reference (103 §4(c)(i)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection correlated the limitation(s) identified as basis of noncompliance to the primary reference (or, if not discussed, assume primary reference is relied on).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rejection does not correlate or discuss a limitation, assume the primary reference is being relied upon for that limitation. Options include: primary reference, secondary reference, Official Notice (well-known/common knowledge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation to secondary reference (103 §4(c)(i)(A)2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection correlated the limitation(s) to a secondary reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the rejection expressly relies on a secondary reference for a limitation. Must be considered along with whether mapping/citation exists for the missing limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on Official Notice (103 §4(c)(i)(A)3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection relies on Official Notice (e.g., 'well known; common knowledge') to meet a limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the rejection relies on any statement that knowledge is known without providing supporting evidence; this can be a basis for noncompliance. The reviewer should capture improper or unsupported use of Official Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: No citation/mapping to prior art for the missing limitation (103 §4(c)(i)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection provides no guidance or citation mapping between the claimed limitation and the applied prior art for the limitation that is the basis for noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This box captures failures to provide any citation/mapping guidance. Degree of correlation is not considered—focus solely on whether guidance exists. Examples: (1) rejection points to a figure but no teaching for limitation C — if some correlation was provided to primary ref, don't check; (2) rejection asserts limitation B is taught by Jones but provides no correlation — check this box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapped but cited portions do not provide sufficient evidence for the limitation (103 §4(c)(i)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection maps a limitation to the prior art, but the cited/referenced portions do not actually provide sufficient evidence to meet that limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is for situations where some correlation/mapping exists but the referenced portions fail to support the limitation. Evaluation is not dependent on amount of mapping—check when mapping exists but is insufficient. Example: rejection points to Figure 1 for limitations A, B, C but Figure 1 lacks teaching for C; check C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection does not adequately articulate how prior art is modified (103 §4(c)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection fails to clearly articulate how the primary reference is being modified to arrive at the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box captures insufficient articulation of the modification step(s). Consult compliance standard and scenarios for fact patterns that rise to noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection lacks a proper reason/rationale/motivation for modification (103 §4(c)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection does not articulate an appropriate reason, motivation, or rationale for modifying the prior art to arrive at the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no persuasive reason or rationale is articulated, check this box. Sub-bases include: prior art does not support the combination (nonanalogous/teaches away), impermissible hindsight, or no articulated reason present. Further checks capture those sub-reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art does not support the asserted combination / nonanalogous art or teaches away (103 §4(c)(iii)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior art applied does not support the claimed combination (e.g., nonanalogous art or art that teaches away from the asserted modification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when there would be no reason to make the asserted modification. This includes art being nonanalogous, teaching away, or modification would destroy the reference being modified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion relies on impermissible hindsight (103 §4(c)(iii)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The conclusion of obviousness relied on impermissible hindsight rather than proper reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check where the rejection's rationale improperly uses knowledge of the claimed invention to read back into the prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: No articulated reason or rationale present (103 §4(c)(iii)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection contains no articulated reason or rationale for the proposed combination/modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the rejection asserts obviousness without providing any motivating rationale. This is distinct from flawed rationale (use other boxes as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper reliance on case law (103 §4(c)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection improperly relies on case law in a way that renders the rejection noncompliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the rejection's use of precedent is misplaced or does not support the rejection in the instant fact pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary considerations rebut obviousness (103 §4(c)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of secondary considerations, the finding of obviousness is improper because the prima facie case is convincingly rebutted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when evidence of secondary considerations (e.g., commercial success, long-felt but unresolved need) rebuts the prima facie case; capture this as a basis for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of noncompliance guidance (103)
rubrics_metrics.description: How the reviewer should write the explanation of noncompliance (scope, tone, specificity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be limited to the basis for noncompliance (e.g., failed identification or insufficient evidence). Avoid rhetorical questions and personalization. When lack of sufficient evidence is asserted, identify each claim and claim limitation forming the basis, explain how the reference fails to meet the limitation(s), or why an interpretation is inappropriate if correlation exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Data/Feedback: improper reliance on inherency (103 §5(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Check when the rejection relies on inherency to meet a claim limitation and that reliance is asserted to be improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only check when the rejection provides an explicit assertion that limitations are met by inherency and that assertion is improper. Do not check when inherency is only implied and not expressly relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Data/Feedback: improper use of Official Notice (103 §5(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Check when there is an improper use of Official Notice in the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to capture improper invocation of Official Notice as the basis for meeting limitations without evidentiary support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Data/Feedback: non-compliance due to unreasonable claim interpretation (103 §5(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-compliance is the result of an unreasonable claim interpretation used by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check only when the rejection provides some guidance or indicates how the limitation is being construed so as to read on the prior art and that construction is unreasonable. If the claim interpretation is not discernible, do not check this box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Data/Feedback: 103 non-compliance inherited from 102 (103 §5(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The 35 U.S.C. 103 noncompliance issue was solely inherited from a noncompliant 102 rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check only when the 103 noncompliance is clearly inherited from a prior noncompliant 102 rejection and not due to another issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Data/Feedback: Part of a '102/103' rejection (103 §5(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection under review is part of a '102/103' rejection and both rejections must be assessed separately for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing a combined '102/103' rejection, complete both the 102 Rejection Made section and the 103 Rejection Made section. Do not check this box if the 102 and 103 rejections are presented separately (not in '102/103' format).

rubrics_metrics.name: 103 Rejections: optional comments / suggested compliant rejection (103 §6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional area for reviewer suggestions, feedback, best practices, or suggested compliant prior art rejections for TC consideration, provided these comments are not directed to the basis of noncompliance (which belongs in Question 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments here should not repeat noncompliance holdings from Question 4. Providing suggested compliant rejections for TC consideration is permissible and optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic: addresses substantially all claims individually (103 characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection addresses substantially all claims individually and only groups claims together that are of substantially similar scope (limited claim lumping).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the rejection treats claims individually where appropriate and limits claim grouping to substantially similar-scope claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic: reasonably pinpoints where limitations are met (103 characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection reasonably pinpoints where substantially all limitations are met by the prior art (e.g., written specification; drawings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the rejection points to precise locations where the reference teaches the claim limitations. Do not check when the rejection refers to large portions of the reference or generally to a figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic: includes pasted pertinent figures with annotations (103 characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection includes pasted pertinent figures with annotations (as appropriate) which pinpoint where limitations are met by the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when pasted annotated figures meaningfully aid in mapping claim limitations to the prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic: goes beyond pinpointing by summarizing how/why limitations are met (103 characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection goes beyond pinpointing by summarizing how/why the limitations are met by the prior art or reciting terminology from the prior art to equate terminology with the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this box is checked, the 'reasonably pinpoints' box should also be checked. This indicates the rejection not only maps but explains how/why the mapping supports the limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic: articulates reasonable rationale for each modification (103 characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection articulates a reasonable rationale for each modification, individually addressing each modification with a separate rationale as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the rejection explains why each asserted modification would have been made and why it is reasonable to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic: statements of patentable weight included (103 characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements of patentable weight are included, particularly when patentable weight is not being given to intended use limitations, preamble, or claim language that suggests or makes optional some structure or steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check where the rejection sets forth whether patentable weight is (or is not) being given to particular claim language elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic: sets forth claim interpretation used (e.g., BRI) (103 characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection sets forth a claim interpretation that points out how the examiner is interpreting the claim/term/phrase for purposes of the rejection (e.g., BRI, special definitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the office action includes explicit claim interpretation relevant to the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic: 112(f) limitations — prior art structure same or equivalent (103 characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: For limitations which invoke 112(f), the rejection explains how the prior art structure was either the same as the disclosed corresponding structure or an equivalent thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check only when the rejection's body explicitly states the prior-art structure is the same or equivalent to the disclosed corresponding structure for a 112(f)-invoking term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic: included detailed legal analysis (103 characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The office action included detailed legal analysis of applicable legal issues through a detailed analysis of the claim(s) and the case law/policy that applies thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the rejection contains substantive legal reasoning tied to the claims and applicable law or policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic: included detailed technical analysis (103 characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The office action included detailed technical analysis regarding the invention and/or the applicability of the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check where meaningful technical analysis supports why the prior art does (or does not) meet the claim limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic: included appropriate suggestions to overcome rejections (103 characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office action included appropriate suggestions to overcome rejection(s) (not general FP language or mere indication of claims with allowable subject matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the OA provides concrete, actionable suggestions for overcoming the rejection, not just boilerplate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic: none of the above (103 characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the listed positive characteristics are present in the 103 rejection(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when no characteristic boxes apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there an accolade related to 103 rejection(s)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the 103 rejection(s) meet the criteria for an accolade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any 103 rejections were NOT in compliance or 'none of the above' is checked for characteristics, this question will not be available. When available, consult current accolade procedures and guidance; complete the provided sentence per accolade procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Were all the 35 U.S.C. 112(a) Enablement rejection(s) in compliance?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether each 112(a) enablement rejection properly identifies the claim(s), the statute, and is supported by sufficient evidence to support the conclusion of lack of enablement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes or No. Use statutory compliance standard and scenarios for assistance. If No, proceed to identify noncompliant claims and bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify claims with non-compliant 112(a) Enablement rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: List each claim discussed individually as a basis for the noncompliance and identify whether the noncompliance is directed to limitations introduced in independent claims, dependent claims, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each claim and indicate the claim type where the basis of noncompliance first appears in the claim tree (only one of independent/dependent/both). Include dependent claims that inherit the noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Was another compliant 112(a) Enablement rejection applied? (112(a) Q3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims identified as having a noncompliant 112(a) rejection, indicate whether another compliant 112(a) enablement rejection was applied to those claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If every listed claim also has another compliant basis, answer Yes; if even one does not, answer No. An individual claim may have multiple bases for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) noncompliance: failure to identify claims/statute (112(a) §4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection does not properly identify the rejected claim(s) and/or identify the correct statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not check when the issue is insufficient evidence (use 4(b)). Do not use this to capture omitted written description rejections—raise omitted rejections separately. Explanations should avoid rhetorical questions and personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) noncompliance: insufficient evidence of lack of enablement (112(a) §4(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection does not set forth sufficient evidence as to why one of ordinary skill in the art could not reasonably make and use the invention without undue experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If checked, at least one of 4(b)(i)–4(b)(iv) must be checked. Consult statutory compliance scenarios for assistance in determining sufficiency of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) basis: rejection based on scope of enablement (112(a) §4(b)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection was based on scope of enablement (examples include unclaimed essential subject matter and single means claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: MPEP 2164.08(c), 2172.01 for unclaimed essential subject matter; MPEP 2164.08(a) for single means claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) basis: Wands factor analysis needed and not provided (112(a) §4(b)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Wands factor analysis was needed to support the enablement rejection but the examiner did not provide it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the rejection asserts lack of enablement but omits the Wands analysis required to support undue experimentation conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) basis: Wands factor analysis provided but insufficiently evidenced/weighted (112(a) §4(b)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Wands factor analysis was provided, but the factors were not sufficiently evidenced and/or weighted to support the conclusion of lack of enablement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when a Wands analysis appears but lacks evidentiary support or appropriate weighting of factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) basis: none of the above (112(a) §4(b)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the listed sub-bases for insufficient evidence apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of 4(b)(i)-4(b)(iii) apply, check this box and provide explanation in the comment box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of noncompliance guidance (112(a) enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: How the reviewer should write the explanation for lack of sufficient evidence for enablement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only comments directed to the basis for noncompliance should be included. Provide explanation consistent with boxes checked under 4(b). Avoid rhetorical questioning and personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Information/Feedback (112(a) enablement) — analysis more appropriate for written description (112(a) §5(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Check when the analysis in the rejection was more appropriate for a written description rejection rather than enablement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This captures mischaracterization of the proper statutory basis for the problems identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Information/Feedback (112(a) enablement) — primarily questions to applicant (112(a) §5(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Check when the analysis primarily consists of questions to applicant rather than an analysis of enablement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejections should analyze enablement, not merely pose questions. Capture that deficiency here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Information/Feedback (112(a) enablement) — unreasonable claim interpretation (112(a) §5(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-compliance is the result of an unreasonable claim interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when claim construction used in the enablement analysis is unreasonable and is the root cause of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Information/Feedback (112(a) enablement) — 112(f) related (112(a) §5(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The 112(a) rejection(s) is 112(f) related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate when the enablement rejection issue ties to 112(f) functional claim elements and corresponding structure/equivalents issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Information/Feedback (112(a) enablement) — deposit of biological material (112(a) §5(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection is related to a deposit of biological material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check where biological deposit issues are germane to the enablement analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) Enablement comments / best practices (112(a) §6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional comments to provide suggestions, feedback, or best practices to the examiner unrelated to the specific noncompliance basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments here should not restate the noncompliance holdings from Question 4. Providing suggestions/best practices is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 112(a) Enablement rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist of characteristics that may be exemplified in enablement rejections (address claims individually, Wands analysis, claim interpretation, legal analysis, suggestions to overcome).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check all applicable boxes. Presence of a characteristic indicates presence, not effectiveness. For example: addresses substantially all claims individually; provides citations to relevant portions of spec and a thorough Wands-factor discussion; sets forth claim interpretation; includes detailed legal analysis; includes appropriate suggestions to overcome rejections; or none of the above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there an accolade related to 112(a) Enablement?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the 112(a) enablement rejection(s) meet criteria for an accolade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any 112(a) rejections were NOT in compliance or 'none of the above' is checked for characteristics, accolade question is not available. When available, consult accolade procedures and complete required sentence per guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Were all the 35 U.S.C. 112(a) Written Description rejection(s) in compliance?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether each 112(a) written description rejection properly identifies the claim(s), the statute, and is supported by sufficient evidence to support the conclusion of lack of written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes or No. Use statutory compliance standards and scenarios for assistance. If No, continue to identify noncompliant claims and provide reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify claims with non-compliant 112(a) Written Description rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: List each claim discussed individually as a basis for the written description noncompliance and indicate whether the noncompliance is directed to limitations introduced in independent claims, dependent claims, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine the type of claim where the limitation first appears in the claim tree and check only one of independent/dependent/both. Include dependent claims that inherit the noncompliance; provide examples to illustrate.

rubrics_metrics.name: For multi-basis written-description rejections: whether another compliant written-description rejection exists (112(a) Q3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims identified as having a noncompliant written-description rejection, indicate whether another compliant 112(a) written-description rejection was applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If every listed claim also has another compliant basis for written-description rejection, answer Yes; otherwise answer No. An individual claim may have multiple bases for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description noncompliance: failure to identify claims/statute (112(a) written description §4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) does not properly identify the rejected claim(s) and/or identify the correct statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box 4(a) is not to capture when the reviewer concludes the claims listed are not properly rejected due to lack of evidence; use 4(b) for evidentiary insufficiency. Avoid using 4(a) to capture omitted rejections; consult statutory compliance standard and scenarios.
